topics.name: Getting around
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: How do people living here usually get around, and which stops or services do they use?
checkInPerson: Walk the route to the stop or station at the times you would travel.
Check whether the stop has a shelter, lighting and step-free access.
Look at the posted timetable at the stop.

topics.name: Everyday places
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Which {subject} do people living here use, and how far away is it?
checkInPerson: Visit at the times you would normally shop or use services.
Check how the walk feels on the way there and back, including the paths and crossings.
If you need a GP surgery, dentist or childcare provider, ask whether it is taking new registrations.

topics.name: Places of worship
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Which {subject} do people living here use, and how do they get there?
checkInPerson: Visit during a service or event time to see how busy the street gets.
Check access and parking nearby at the times that matter to you.

topics.name: Schools
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Which schools do children living here usually go to, and how are places decided?
checkInPerson: Visit the school during a normal day, or at an open event.
Walk the route you would take with your child at school drop-off time.
Ask the school how places were allocated in the most recent year.

topics.name: Family view
checkInPerson: Visit childcare and a school during opening hours.
Walk the routes with a child at the time they would travel.
Visit the nearest park at different times of day.
topics.note: A grouping that reuses childcare, school and park records already counted under other topics. Never in the counts.

topics.name: Planning nearby
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Are there any planning applications or building work planned near the home?
checkInPerson: Walk past the site and note any notices displayed on or near it.
Look at the building work or empty plots around the home.
Check the council planning page for later updates.

topics.name: Flood
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Has the home or the street ever flooded, and is there a flood history for the property?
checkInPerson: Look at where water would run: the lowest points of the street and the ground around the home.
Ask neighbours about past flooding.
Look for damp marks, tide lines or flood protection on the property.

topics.name: Recorded crime
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: What is the area like at different times of day, and what do people living here say about it?
checkInPerson: Visit in the evening and at the weekend as well as in the daytime.
Look at lighting and how the street is used at different times.
Talk to people who live nearby.

topics.name: Sold nearby
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Can you tell me about homes that have sold nearby recently and how they compare?
checkInPerson: Compare the sold homes you can see with the home you are looking at.
Ask an agent how the sold homes differ in size and condition.

topics.name: Broadband
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Which broadband provider and speed do people living here use, and how reliable is it?
checkInPerson: Check the speed on your own device in the rooms you would work in.
Ask the current occupant what they use and what they pay.
Check that the lines or sockets in the home are in place.

topics.name: Air quality
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: What is the air like around the home on busy days and at busy times of day?
checkInPerson: Visit at rush hour and note traffic and smell.
Look at how close the home is to main roads or industrial sites.
Check whether the windows can be opened comfortably on the road side.

topics.name: Radon
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Has radon been measured in the home, and what was the result?
checkInPerson: Ask the owner or landlord whether radon has been measured in the home, and ask to see the result.
Ask whether anything has been fitted to reduce radon.

topics.name: Council tax by band
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Does this council area have a parish or town council charge on top of the council's own charge for each band?
checkInPerson: Look at the council's own council tax page for this year's charge for each band, including any parish or town council charge.

topics.name: Housing affordability
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: How do house prices here compare with what people earn locally, and how has that changed?
checkInPerson: Compare the home's monthly cost with your own income.
Look at what similar homes nearby cost to buy or rent.

topics.name: Deprivation
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: What should I know about the neighbourhood that published figures do not show?
checkInPerson: Walk through the neighbourhood at different times and see how it is looked after.
Talk to people who live nearby about the area.
Look at the local shops, services and community spaces.

topics.name: Transport connectivity
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: How do people living here usually travel for work and school?
checkInPerson: Try a real journey to your workplace or school at the time you would travel.
Check the service for late evening and weekend trips.
Look at how easy it is to reach the stop or station on foot.

topics.name: Green space
topics.gapQuestionTemplate: Which green spaces can the public use near the home, and what are they like?
checkInPerson: Walk to the nearest green space and see how it is kept.
Check the entrances, paths and opening times.
Visit at a weekend to see how busy it is.

topics.name: Council tax band of a home
checkInPerson: Ask for the latest council tax bill for the home.
Check the band on the official page for the exact address.

officialRoute.label: Check the council tax band of a home (gov.uk)

topics.name: Energy certificate of a home
checkInPerson: Ask the owner or landlord for the energy certificate number, which is printed on the certificate.
Check the certificate on the official page, and look at its date.

topics.name: Mobile by network
checkInPerson: Check signal on your own phone in each room.
Ask the current occupant which network they use and what it is like in each room.
Try a call and a video call in the rooms you would use most.

topics.name: Noise
checkInPerson: Visit at rush hour, in the evening and at night.
Listen with the windows open and closed.
Note any flight paths, railway lines or busy roads you can hear.

officialRoute.label: Government road and rail noise mapping (gov.uk)

topics.name: Ground and mining
checkInPerson: Look for cracks in walls or uneven floors.
Ask whether a mining or ground search was done.

officialRoute.label: Check if a property is affected by coal mining (gov.uk)
